title: OT-RRDE v0.3 pilot mapping to CERT/CC SSVC
comparison_conventions: Each SSVC input carries its own value, evidence and rationale. Null is an unresolved input and withholds an exact tree outcome.
The pinned CERT/CC exposure default is applied as Open to unknown paths and labelled as a default. Controlled mappings retain their provisional analyst status.
Exploitation None requires the dossier to document adequate checking for public exploit code or a well-known method, in addition to its observations about active exploitation.
Deployment rating scope follows the existing study protocol's applicable-and-deployable patch endpoint. It is tracked separately from completeness of the priority-tree inputs.
Investigation urgency and deployment priority are separate endpoints. Both are reported in their native categories.
A direct judgement of decision quality requires independent ratings and the same scorable pairs.

ssvc:E:1.1.0.basis: The in-time fictional catalogue records exploitation in the wild for the finding.

ssvc:EXP:1.0.1.basis: The structured case declares a verified controlled path. Controlled is a provisional mapping whose access restrictions and attack-path details need clarification.

ssvc:A:2.0.0.basis: The dossier supplies no exploit mechanics or chain evidence sufficient to assess reliable automation of reconnaissance, weaponisation, delivery and exploitation.

ssvc:HI:2.0.2.basis: The dossier gives broad safety and availability labels. An organisation-specific mission assessment and a safety-impact assessment under the SSVC definitions are required to select Human Impact.

deployment_rating_scope.basis: Availability-impact review awaits sign-off, so the study's applicable-and-deployable patch endpoint is pending.

cases.interpretation_note: Mappings were authored after the pilot case design and require independent criticism.
